assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a superconducting artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon in a resonator, opening a clean, controllable regime of light-matter physics (strong coupling, dispersive readout, photon-number resolved measurement, quantum-state engineering). It is the architecture underlying most superconducting quantum processors, but the prize-worthy point is the new regime of quantum optics on a chip. Seen as a theorist embedded in experiments, I regard it as a very clear, originality-rich discovery that follows naturally on the 2025 circuit-tunnelling prize without duplicating it. I declare my proximity to this field and defer partly to colleagues on weighing it.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal (Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin, Schoelkopf) and the 2004 Yale experiment are the core. Schoelkopf (experiment and leadership of the Yale group) and Girvin (theory) are decisive; Blais is first author of the theory paper. Andreas Wallraff, who performed the strong-coupling experiment, is not in the supplied credited names, so the supplied credit may under-represent the experimental side, and I cannot add him.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently and repeatedly across many laboratories over two decades, with a stable interpretation and wide technological uptake. Recognition is timely, with no sign of premature judgement; the main timing question is how soon after the 2025 prize the committee wants to return to superconducting circuits.
uncertainties: Wallraff is not among the credited names and may be a necessary contributor to a fair experimental credit.
Possible overlap with the 2025 prize may make the committee reluctant to go back to superconducting circuits so soon.
My own proximity to the field could bias my ranking upward; I am recalling the literature from memory and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposals for quantum gates with trapped ions and for analog and digital quantum simulation with cold atoms laid the theoretical foundation for two experimental platforms that now run programmable quantum devices. The originality is high, the ideas are crisp, and they translated directly into experiments (ion-trap gates, Hubbard-model simulation with optical lattices, Rydberg and other schemes). This is foundational physics that turned into an enabling platform, as I like to see.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are clearly the two decisive theorists, with a long record of joint and individual proposals (1995 ion-trap gate, 1998 Jaksch-Zoller optical lattice proposal). A two-person prize is natural. A fair prize would likely also have to acknowledge experimentalists such as Wineland, who is already recognised, so the boundary with prior prizes is clean.
assessment.maturity: The proposals have been realised and confirmed by many independent groups over three decades; the interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the first ion-trap gate proposal versus subsequent refinements, and overlap with the already recognised 2012 prize for ion control, requires careful wording of the citation.
Overlap of Zoller with the optical-lattice candidate may require a decision about which candidate carries him.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength idea and its realisation at fractional uncertainties of order 1e-18, is a clean experiment where every physical detail (blackbody shifts, collisions, lattice light shifts) is understood. It has opened precision tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second. Originality and lasting impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept (2001-2003) and realised the Sr clock; Jun Ye brought it to the highest accuracy and developed many-body and comb-linked clocks. Two laureates is a fair, compact configuration. Other groups (e.g. Lemonde, Hollberg, Ludlow, Hinkley) contributed but are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, with many independent clocks (Sr, Yb, others) agreeing with each other at the 1e-18 level. Recognition is timely, though the redefinition of the second is still pending, which does not weaken the discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognise a precision-measurement achievement relative to a discovery.
Priority questions between the Katori and other proposals for lattice clocks I cannot settle from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat moire bands at the magic angle and experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a new field of tunable moire quantum matter. It is original, highly visible and widely reproduced. As a non-specialist in materials I defer to colleagues but see a clear prediction-to-experiment story.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the 2018 experimental discoveries. This maps naturally onto a three-person prize, although other contributors, such as Cao, Fatemi, and others, are not credited or are not senior leaders.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories since 2018 with rich follow-up (fractional Chern insulators, ferromagnetism), but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the strongly correlated phases is not settled, so the interpretation is still evolving. Recognition is plausible but may be slightly early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is unresolved.
Sample-to-sample variation and reproducibility of correlated states.
Credit for related theory (e.g. Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto; Suarez Morell) is not captured by the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson by ATLAS and CMS confirmed the last missing piece of the Standard Model and is a landmark of experimental physics, with unambiguous importance. It is outside my area, so I defer to particle physicists on the weighting.
assessment.attribution: The decisive contributions are collective. The supplied names (spokespeople and designers of the detectors, plus the LHC director) are a plausible but inevitably contested subset; the three-person limit makes a fair configuration difficult. I pick three leaders of the experiments, leaving Lyn Evans (accelerator) and Michel Della Negra out, which is a judgement that can be questioned.
assessment.maturity: The Higgs discovery in 2012 is thoroughly confirmed and its properties have been measured in many channels; the discovery side is mature. The theory was already recognised in 2013.
uncertainties: Allocation among collaboration leaders versus accelerator builders is intrinsically disputed.
I am relying on general knowledge rather than detailed knowledge of the experimental leadership history.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cold-atom quantum simulation of strongly correlated matter, such as the superfluid-Mott insulator transition in optical lattices, Fermi-Hubbard physics and single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopes, makes many-body quantum phenomena visible and controllable. This is the type of clean experiment that I value, and it already guides understanding of strongly interacting systems.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch made the Mott transition experiment, Bloch and Esslinger pursued fermionic and many-body simulation, and Greiner developed the quantum gas microscope. Zoller (theory) is credited but I place him in the separate Cirac-Zoller candidate to avoid duplication. Hanns-Christoph Nagerl, Gross and others are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely replicated, although quantum advantage over classical simulation for the hardest regimes such as the doped Fermi-Hubbard model remains open. Recognition seems timely.
uncertainties: Choosing between Zoller and Esslinger or others for the third laureate slot.
Open question whether simulations have solved problems beyond classical reach.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators, from the quantum spin Hall prediction to the observation in HgTe and the quantum anomalous Hall effect in magnetic topological insulators, introduced a conceptually new classification of electronic matter with robust edge transport. Importance and clarity are high.
assessment.attribution: Kane (theory, with Mele), Molenkamp (observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe, with Konig and others after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal) and Xue (quantum anomalous Hall) are plausible. The theory credit is contested because Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang and Mele are also decisive, and Zhang is deceased, which makes a fair configuration difficult.
assessment.maturity: Well-confirmed experimentally, but the practical application remains limited and the quantum anomalous Hall effect still requires very low temperatures. Recognition would be mature.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among Kane, Mele, Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, and Fu is disputed and Mele is not in this list's names.
The compound nature (theory, spin Hall in HgTe, anomalous Hall in magnetic films) may need separate recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cavity optomechanics, including sideband cooling to the quantum ground state and the quantum control of mechanical motion with light or microwaves, brought mechanical resonators into the quantum regime and links closely to the circuit-QED toolbox I know. Importance is considerable, especially for quantum limits of measurement and transduction.
assessment.attribution: Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer are the leading figures in the optomechanics field and ground-state cooling; Vahala contributed the early microcavity radiation-pressure work. Excluding Vahala gives a two-person configuration whose fairness is debatable. Other major contributors, such as Painter, Lehnert, Cleland, and Schwab, are not credited.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed by several groups, but the field is still rapidly developing and the field-defining achievements are partly overlapping with the 2025 and the 2012 prizes on quantum control of macroscopic systems. It may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum phenomena in devices and the 2012 prize on controlling single quantum systems.
Credit conflict for the early radiation pressure cooling work, which includes names not supplied.
